evidence: Figure 2.2 caption, book page 32 (PDF p.56): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — both plotted intensities are computed from the stated inputs, not measured"
issue: Provenance label mismatch. The Preface (p.14) defines [ILLUSTRATIVE] as "a non-canonical worked example or scenario input chosen to make a calculation concrete" and [canonical scenario] as "the book's own internally defined workload and model (Ch. 4, Table 4-2)." Both plotted intensities — prefill ~9,200 FLOP/byte (= 1.29 PFLOP / 140 GB) and decode ~1 FLOP/byte (= 140 GFLOP / 140 GB) — are computed from the canonical scenario's own inputs (Table 4-2: 70B model, 9,200 tokens, FP16, H100 specs). The caption itself says they are "computed from the stated inputs." Per the Preface's rule (p.16: "a value arithmetically derived from those assumed inputs ... is [canonical scenario][DERIVED]"), the correct provenance should be [canonical scenario][DERIVED], not [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The same pattern recurs on Figure 1.1 (PDF p.56, "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch. 4, Table 4-2)") and Figure 2.1 (PDF p.44, "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch 4)") — all three label canonical-scenario-derived content with the non-canonical provenance tag.
fix_instruction: Change [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] to [canonical scenario][DERIVED] on Figure 2.2's caption where the label specifically attributes to "both plotted intensities." For Figures 1.1 and 2.1, where [ILLUSTRATIVE] may describe the schematic artifact (a simplified drawing) rather than the data, either add a clarifying note that [ILLUSTRATIVE] refers to the drawing's simplification (not the data provenance) or restructure the label to separate figure-artifact provenance from data provenance. Recurrence sweep: check all figure captions that carry [ILLUSTRATIVE] but whose plotted/drawn values derive from Table 4-2.

evidence: Table 2-2, "Prefill: FLOPs, linear term only" row, derivation column: "2 ×70e9 ×9.2e3 ≈ 1.29 ×10¹⁵; excludes the quadratic attention term, which adds ~0.22 PFLOP (+17%) at 9.2K → ~1.51 PFLOP total, Ch 8 case (ii)"
issue: Inconsistent rounding precision for the same quantity across locations. Table 2-2 (PDF p.30) states the attention-term contribution as "(+17%)" (no decimal places), while the Table 2-2 scope note on the same page states "~0.22 PFLOP (+17.23%)" (two decimal places). Recomputed: 0.222e15 / 1.288e15 = 17.23%. Both values are arithmetically correct at their respective precision, but quoting 17% and 17.23% for the same figure in adjacent text blocks (both within Table 2-2's scope note) is inconsistent presentation — a reader comparing the table row to its own scope note sees two different precisions for one quantity. Note: this is a presentation inconsistency, not an arithmetic error.
fix_instruction: Standardize the precision of the attention-term percentage within Table 2-2. Either use "~17%" in both the table row and the scope note, or use "~17.2%" in both. The table row already uses "~" so a rounded value is expected; the scope note's two-decimal precision is the outlier.

evidence: Section 7.3.2 (book page 149, PDF p.173): "At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB (17,179,869,184 B ≈ 17.18 GB on the chapter's decimal GB basis, §7.1). This analytical result assumes one sequence and unsharded raw tensors." Followed by: "[1P][FACT] for the configuration; [1P][DERIVED] for the storage."
issue: Missing provenance label for the chosen context length input. The storage figure (16 GiB at 262,144 tokens) is labeled [1P][DERIVED] — correctly derived from the Qwen3.8-27B configuration ([1P][FACT]). However, 262,144 tokens is a deliberately chosen context-length input for the calculation, not a value stated in the Qwen3.8-27B configuration. Per the Preface (p.14): "[ASSUMPTION] — a deliberately chosen scenario input" and per the exception test (p.15): "a number that any downstream figure depends on is labeled." The same applies to the 131,072-token figure in the next paragraph: "At 131,072 tokens the same component is 8 GiB (8,589,934,592 B ≈ 8.59 GB decimal)." Neither context length carries its own provenance/epistemic label — they are chosen inputs that should carry an [ASSUMPTION] tag (or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] if non-canonical) alongside the [1P][DERIVED] storage figure.
fix_instruction: Add provenance labels for the chosen context lengths: e.g., change "At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB" to explicitly label 262,144 as an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] input (or [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] if it belongs to the canonical set — but it doesn't appear in Table 4-2, so [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] is correct). Similarly for 131,072. The [1P][FACT] and [1P][DERIVED] labels already on the configuration and storage respectively can remain; add the missing label for the input.
